7.5.2.2 Transmit Data via ’Decoupled Buffer Access’ Mode
Figure 7.8 depicts the internal processing for data transmission in principle14 if "Decou-
pled Buffer Access" mode is configured15. Below there is a description of the different
steps which are necessary to transmit data via FrTp.
14Figure 7.8 depicts only the overview of data transmission for a single channel without further func-
tionality (e.g. transmit cancellation) or internal behaviour (e.g. internal control data handling, return
values etc.). Also a schedule for data transfer in concurrent channels is not described here.
15Buffer access mode is configured for each N-PDU (refer to FrIf) and is referenced via the PDU-Pool.
PduR
FrTp
LSduR
FrIf
01. FrTp_Transmit (TxSDU-ID, …)
02. Evaluate TxSDU-ID
03. Allocate fee channel and set connection
04. Set Flag TX_SDU_AVAILABLE (TxSDU-ID)
05. FrTp_Main
06. Call routine PduR_FrTpCopyTxData (TxSDU-ID, ..)
07. Allocate fee TxPDU-ID
08. Call routine PduR_FrTpCopyTxData (TxSDU-ID, ..)
09. Prepare Address Information and PCI
10. Call routine LSduR_FrTpTransmit (TxPDU-ID)
14. LSduR_FrTpTxConfirmation
11. Call routine FrIf_Transmit (TxPDU-ID)
15. Call routine FrTp_TxConfirmation and set TxPduState = „Idle“
16. FrTp_Main
IF:
17. FlowControl reception is expected
THEN:
18. Wait until FlowControl is received
ELSE:
19. Continue at Step 20
IF:
20. All SDU data transmitted
THEN:
21. Free Channel
22. Reset Flag TX_SDU_AVAILABLE
23. Call Pdu_TxConfirmation (TxSDU-ID, ..)
ELSE:
24. Continue at Step 8

Figure 7.8: Transmit data overview in ’Decoupled Buffer Access’ mode
Step 01 - 10
Step 01 - 10 in ’decoupled access mode’ are equal to step 01 - 10 in ’immediate access
mode’. Please refer to Chapter 7.5.2.1.
For step 09 it is recommended to set the address information and PCI to a local buffer
because the service primitive FrTp_TriggerTransmit is called in interrupt mode
